gloss: Urashima Tarō (folk-tale hero); someone out of touch after a long absence

definitions.explanation: The fisherman of a famous Japanese folk tale who saves a turtle, is taken to the undersea Dragon Palace, and returns home to find that hundreds of years have passed. When he opens the box he was told never to open, he becomes an old man.

definitions.gloss: someone out of touch after a long absence
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively for a person who comes back after a long time away (abroad, in hospital, out of contact) and finds the world changed, like a Japanese Rip Van Winkle. Often in the phrase {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}の{気分|きぶん}だ or {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}{状態|じょうたい}.

examples.japanese: {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧カメ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{助|たす}けた→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧。
{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{竜宮城|りゅうぐうじょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Urashima Tarō went to the Dragon Palace.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頃|ころ}→頃：32850_koro⟧、⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, my grandmother often read me the story of Urashima Tarō.

examples.japanese: ⟦まるで→まるで：03739_marude⟧{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}だ。
examples.english: I feel just like Urashima Tarō.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}ぶり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{帰国|きこく}して→帰国する：21786_kikokusuru⟧{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧だ。
examples.english: Back in Japan after ten years, I'm completely out of touch.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{入院|にゅういん}していた→入院する：01849_nyuuinsuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{退院|たいいん}したら→退院する：01847_taiinsuru⟧{浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧だった。
examples.english: I had been in hospital so long that when I came out I felt like Urashima Tarō.

notes:
One of the best-known Japanese folk tales; every child knows it from picture books and the school song that begins むかしむかし{浦島|うらしま}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧: being out of touch after a long absence
- {浦島太郎|うらしまたろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧: feeling like Urashima Tarō
- {竜宮城|りゅうぐうじょう}: the Dragon Palace under the sea
- {玉手箱|たまてばこ}: the box he must not open; by extension, a box full of surprises

CULTURAL NOTE:
The figurative use is about time and change, not about sleeping: the English "Rip Van Winkle" is the closest match.
